solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Car generally admired by Chinese Tesla dealer

parts.note: a Merc is the familiar short name for a Mercedes, a car widely admired
the Han are China's majority people
T is the symbol for the tesla, the SI unit of magnetic flux density

explanation.surface: A Chinese car dealer looks up to a car admired everywhere, while selling Teslas.
explanation.walkthrough: Tesla looks like the car maker, but here it is the physics unit, abbreviated T.
explanation.definitionFit: A merchant is a trader who buys and sells goods, a synonym for dealer.

clue.text: Snoopy manoeuvres close to Charlie as pigeon flutters

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter, so the end of Charlie is taken
fluttering suggests a flurry of movement, so the letters of the words that follow are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: Snoopy the cartoon beagle, friend of Charlie Brown, moves about as a pigeon flaps nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flutters' shuffles AS PIGEON into SPIONAGE, after E from the end of Charlie. Snoopy and Charlie suggest Peanuts, but 'Snoopy' is just an adjective here.
explanation.definitionFit: Espionage is spying, and a spy's covert operations are literally snooping moves.

clue.text: Bend over daily for proficiency

indicators.note: in a down clue, over says the word above is turned upside down, read from the bottom

parts.note: an arc is a curve or bend
the FT, the Financial Times, is a daily newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone bends over backwards every day to become skilled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns ARC into CRA; FT is the paper this puzzle appears in.
explanation.definitionFit: Craft means skill or expertise in making or doing something, so proficiency.

clue.text: Mountain range risen in Nepal keeps rising

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising says the letters are read from bottom to top
the phrase keeps the answer within it, so the letters are found inside these words

explanation.surface: A mountain range keeps growing higher in Nepal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeps' signals SENINNEPA held inside 'risen in Nepal', and 'rising' reads it upwards. Nepal suggests the Himalayas, but the range is in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apennines are the chain of mountains running down the length of Italy.

clue.text: Grass turned blue under boss's control

indicators.note: turned round says the word is read backwards

parts.note: pot is slang for cannabis, also called grass
feeling blue means feeling down

explanation.surface: Someone who smoked grass turned miserable under the boss's watch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses POT to TOP.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-down management is run from the top, with direction and decisions coming from the boss.

clue.text: Manual worker playing I-spy between times

indicators.note: between says the scrambled letters sit inside the two outer pieces

parts.note: T is short for time, and plural times gives two Ts

indicators.note: playing suggests playing about with the letters of the game named

explanation.surface: A labourer plays a game of I-spy during breaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges I-SPY into YPIS. Manual looks like physical labour, but a typist works by hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A typist works with the hands at a keyboard, so a manual worker in the literal sense of hand-worker.

clue.text: Try to wind up loo paper when half-cut

indicators.note: cut says letters are cut away from the phrase for loo paper

parts.note: toilet roll is loo paper; loo is British slang for toilet
half stands for five letters, half of the ten in the phrase, taken from just after its first letter

explanation.surface: A drunk tries to wind toilet paper back onto its tube.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' removes OILET, half of the ten letters of TOILET ROLL. Half-cut is British slang for drunk, which is the surface reading.
explanation.definitionFit: To troll is to try to provoke people online, and wind up is British slang for annoy or tease.

clue.text: Tucking into beer, maybe masks pizza's flavour

indicators.note: tucking into says one piece is pushed inside another

parts.note: Peroni is an Italian beer brand
PPE, personal protective equipment, includes masks as one example

explanation.surface: Someone tucking into an Italian beer has their mask hiding the taste of the pizza.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' marks masks as just one example of protective equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepperoni is a spicy sausage used as a classic pizza topping, so it gives a pizza its flavour.

clue.text: Attack upset Miss Otis's father, presumably absent one

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so read from the bottom
absent says a letter is missing from the name

parts.note: the father of a Miss Otis would be Mr Otis
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Miss Otis's absent father, upset, launches an attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absent one' drops I from MROTIS, giving MROTS, and 'upset' reverses it. 'Miss Otis Regrets' is a Cole Porter song.
explanation.definitionFit: To storm a place is to attack it in force, as troops storm a fortress.

clue.text: Happy to see the latest news

parts.note: up means cheerful or in good spirits
to see someone romantically is to date them

explanation.surface: Someone is glad to hear the most recent news.
explanation.definitionFit: An update is a report of the most recent information on something.

clue.text: Ridicule bands making comeback

indicators.note: coming back says the letters run the other way

parts.note: a hoop is a band, and plural bands gives two hoops

explanation.surface: Critics mock bands that try to stage a comeback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making comeback' reverses HOOPHOOP; bands here are rings, not musical groups.
explanation.definitionFit: To pooh-pooh something is to dismiss it scornfully, a near synonym of ridicule.

clue.text: Padding that's firm and dry worn by women, backing up toilet

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
TT, teetotal, means not drinking alcohol
something worn by a person is on them

indicators.note: backing says the word is read backwards

parts.note: loo is British slang for toilet

explanation.surface: A sturdy, dry padding worn by women, which backs up the toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing up' reverses LOO into OOL. Cotton wool is the British term for absorbent cotton.
explanation.definitionFit: Cotton wool, raw fluffy cotton, is used as soft padding and stuffing.

clue.text: Bovary perhaps a Madame you should recall

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the letters are read backwards

explanation.surface: As you should remember, Bovary was a Madame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'you should recall' reverses AMME. Madame Bovary is Flaubert's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Emma Bovary is the heroine of Flaubert's novel, so the first name is an example of a Bovary.

clue.text: Subatomic particle that's surprising PhD by never spinning

parts.note: ha is an exclamation of surprise
a PhD holder is called Dr, doctor

indicators.note: spinning round says the word is turned to face the other way

parts.note: no means never, as in 'no way'

explanation.surface: A particle that astonishes a PhD by refusing to spin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinning' turns NO into ON. 'Spin' is also a particle property, part of the disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: A hadron is a class of subatomic particle, such as a proton or neutron, held together by the strong force.

clue.text: Drill tries going through concrete

indicators.note: going through says one piece passes into the middle of another

parts.note: concrete means actual or real
a judge hears, that is tries, a case

explanation.surface: A drill bit tries to bore through concrete.
explanation.walkthrough: Drill looks like a power tool; it is a practice session, and 'tries' is what a court does.
explanation.definitionFit: A drill is a practice exercise, and a rehearsal is a practice run before a performance.

clue.text: Seventh element that's in caffeine?

parts.note: the element with atomic number seven is part of the caffeine molecule, and the seventh letter of 'caffeine' is its chemical symbol

explanation.surface: A quiz question about what makes up caffeine.
explanation.walkthrough: The seventh letter, or element, of CAFFEINE is N, the symbol for this gas, which caffeine does contain.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitrogen has atomic number seven and is one of the elements in the caffeine molecule.

clue.text: Kind hosts bother making weak batter

indicators.note: hosting a guest means having them inside, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: tender means kind or gentle
to ail is to trouble or bother

explanation.surface: A kindly host gets bothered by a feeble pancake mix.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a tail-ender is one of the last, least skilled batsmen in the order; batter looks like pancake mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Tail-enders bat at the end of a cricket innings because they are the team's poorest batsmen.

clue.text: Letter writer's arm always cramps

indicators.note: to cramp is to confine, so one piece is squeezed inside the other

parts.note: e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, meaning always
a pistol is a firearm, an arm

explanation.surface: A letter writer's arm keeps getting cramp.
explanation.walkthrough: Arm reads as a limb, but it is a weapon; e'er is poetic for ever.
explanation.definitionFit: An epistoler writes epistles, and an epistle is a formal letter.

clue.text: Who the devil is this poem about?

indicators.note: about here means moved about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A reader asks which devilish figure a poem concerns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges THIS POEM. 'Who the devil' looks like an exclamation; it asks for the devil's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Mephisto, short for Mephistopheles, is the devil of the Faust legend.

clue.text: Doctor lasers opening for otoplasty, having no blades

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter
to doctor is to tamper with or alter, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A surgeon uses lasers to begin ear surgery, no scalpels needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' is the rearranging signal. Otoplasty is ear surgery; the blades are the flat ends of oars.
explanation.definitionFit: An oar's blade is its flat end, so a boat lacking oars has no blades.

clue.text: Papers repeated the very thing that was successful

indicators.note: repeated says the papers piece is written a second time straight after the first

parts.note: ID means identity papers
it means the very thing, as in 'that's it'

explanation.surface: Newspapers kept reporting what had worked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeated' doubles the ID. The answer is a cry of triumph, and also leads into 24 down, Sinatra's 'My Way'.
explanation.definitionFit: 'I did it!' is what someone exclaims after an effort that worked out.

clue.text: Yes, gran peeled vegetables

parts.note: OK means yes

indicators.note: peeling removes the outside, so the outer letters are dropped

explanation.surface: Granny agreed and peeled the vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: Okra, also called ladies' fingers, are green seed pods eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Moral lead regularly given by King, a tree-hugger

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for king, as in chess

indicators.note: regularly means taking letters at even intervals, every second one

explanation.surface: A king sets a moral example to an environmentalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tree-hugger' suggests an environmentalist; here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A koala spends its life clinging to eucalyptus trees, so it literally hugs trees.

clue.text: Penny has ordered her tomcat outside for being destructive indoors

indicators.note: outside says the rearranged letters surround the other piece
ordered means put into a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Penny has put her tomcat outdoors for wrecking the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' rearranges HER TOMCAT into CARETMOTH, which goes 'outside' P.
explanation.definitionFit: Carpet moth larvae eat woollen carpets and fabrics, a pest doing damage inside the home.

clue.text: Take it easy when in bed

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
as means when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Relax when you are in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To coast is to move along without effort, so to take it easy.

clue.text: How 20 is a number

definitions.meaning: 20 across is I DID IT, and the song line runs 'I did it ...', so this is how it was done
A song, made famous by Frank Sinatra

explanation.surface: A puzzle question about how one answer counts as a number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is a song here, not a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: 'My Way' is the Sinatra standard whose refrain ends 'I did it my way'.

clue.text: Port artist consumed full of flavour enhancer

indicators.note: full of says the outer pieces contain the other

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
consumed means ate
MSG, monosodium glutamate, is a flavour enhancer

explanation.surface: An artist in a harbour town ate food loaded with MSG.
explanation.walkthrough: Ramsgate is a port town on the Kent coast of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramsgate is a harbour town in Kent, a port with a ferry history.

clue.text: Festival in Shangri-la, widespread to the west

indicators.note: to the west says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the answer lies inside the run of words that follows it

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A festival is held in the paradise of Shangri-la, popular across the West.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the letters within 'Shangri-la, widespread', and 'to the west' reads them right to left, as west is left on a map.
explanation.definitionFit: Diwali is the Hindu festival of lights, celebrated each autumn.

clue.text: Each golfer initially allowed a birdie

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the word

parts.note: to let is to allow

explanation.surface: Each golfer was at first permitted a birdie, one under par.
explanation.walkthrough: Birdie looks like the golf score; it is a small bird, here a young eagle.
explanation.definitionFit: An eaglet is a young eagle, and birdie is a familiar word for a little bird.

clue.text: They shower requests on Santa's head

indicators.note: on says the letter is placed in front of the following word
the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: prayers are requests, as to a god

explanation.surface: Children rain wishes down on Father Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprayers are things that spray liquid over something, which is to shower it.
